players.product: SMR designer (Xe-100) - Doosan Enerbility equity stake and prospective equipment customer

connects_to.relationship: Xe-100 SMR projects to power Amazon's data-center footprint (options for more than 5 GWe by 2039; Energy Northwest first project)

contracts.signal: Prospectus: X-energy names Amazon among its three customers (Dow, Amazon, Centrica). After evaluating carbon-free generation for its data-center footprint, Amazon made an equity investment in X-energy in 2024 and announced options to bring more than 5 GWe of new Xe-100 projects online across the U.S. by 2039; the first deployment is with Energy Northwest (four reactors, 320 MWe, upsizable to 960 MWe). X-energy granted Amazon first-priority allocation of Xe-100 manufacturing queue slots across 2031 to 2039, to allocate to utilities and independent power producers that will own and operate the SMR facilities, a right of first refusal on a portion of scheduled delivery and most-favored pricing (including minimum TRISO-X fuel allocations); Amazon is not obligated to purchase. From the fifth anniversary of the first Amazon-sponsored project's commercial operation, X-energy must pay Amazon amounts reflecting cost efficiencies achieved relative to the initial projects' PPA prices.
contracts.units: more than 5 GWe by 2039; first project four reactors, 320 MWe (up to 960 MWe)

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus customer concentration: the U.S. Government and Dow accounted for 87% and 6% of FY2025 total revenue and grant income (74% and 22% in FY2024). FY2025 revenues and grant income $109,098 thousand (FY2024 $120,152 thousand) - DoE $89,396 thousand, DoD $5,444 thousand, commercial $14,258 thousand; revenue associated with Dow $6,943 thousand (FY2024 $26,848 thousand); net loss $389,778 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. Government 87%; Dow 6% of FY2025 revenue and grant income

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline (prospectus): X-energy says its three customers Dow, Amazon and Centrica provide, assuming each exercises its contingent rights in full, a more than 11 GWe, 144-reactor pipeline across the U.S. and the U.K.; it is working to deliver eight reactors across its first announced sites at Seadrift, Texas (Dow) and Richland, Washington (Energy Northwest / Amazon), with the Amazon / Energy Northwest construction permit application targeted for submission to the NRC by the end of 2026 and the construction permit anticipated in 2028. In March 2026 it signed a non-binding letter of intent with Talen Energy to assess Xe-100 deployment in Pennsylvania and across the PJM market (no binding agreements yet).
quarterly_data.figure: more than 11 GWe, 144-reactor pipeline; eight reactors at the first two sites
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: LOI partner (Xe-100 deployment assessment in PJM)

quarterly_data.signal: Illustrative per-plant economics (prospectus, company assumptions): over a plant's life, customer fees of $2,410 - 4,725 million (reactor technology fee $50 - 300 million, reactor services $800 - 1,300 million, fuel $1,560 - 3,125 million) against costs to X-energy of $1,660 - 2,180 million, a target margin of 30% - 55%; the initial fuel load at commercial operation is about 5% of lifetime fuel needs, with continuous online refueling generating about 90% of fuel revenue over a 60-year design life. X-energy has not yet entered into technology-fee or definitive fuel supply agreements with customers.
quarterly_data.figure: customer fees $2,410 - 4,725 million per plant; target margin 30% - 55%

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier: SGL Carbon announced in January 2026 a 10-year graphite supply agreement for Xe-100 reactor components and has commenced production for the Dow Seadrift plant under an initial three-year award valued at over $100 million (firm-fixed pricing, milestone payments secured by a corporate guarantee). X-energy's unconditional purchase obligations, primarily graphite-component supply agreements, totaled $63,393 thousand ($27,000 thousand due in 2026); it had $17.0 million of deposits for long-lead materials, and FY2025 capital expenditures were $117,236 thousand (FY2024 $4,162 thousand) for new facilities.
quarterly_data.figure: initial three-year graphite award over $100 million; purchase obligations $63,393 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Partners (prospectus): in August 2025 Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) signed a joint compact with X-energy, Amazon and Doosan outlining the intention to collaborate on deploying the Amazon order book in the U.S.; related-party investor Curtiss-Wright received $11.6 million of subcontracting costs in 2025 ($4.2 million in 2024) for DOE ARDP work.

players.product: gas turbines & SMR for data-center power

connects_to.relationship: Doosan Enerbility equity investor in X-Energy and prospective SMR equipment supplier

contracts.signal: Prospectus: Doosan is a preferred strategic supplier to X-energy; in December 2025 it signed a Reservation Agreement committing to build a new SMR fabrication facility and to reserve forging capacity for 16 sets of key pressure-boundary components for the Xe-100 program, for a non-refundable $12 million reservation fee in two $6 million installments creditable against future purchase orders, with a $1.5 million commitment fee per set if purchase orders are not placed on the agreed timeline.
contracts.units: forging capacity for 16 sets of pressure-boundary components
contracts.value: $12 million reservation fee; $1.5 million per set commitment fee
